chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Asama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
From the Sunnah of the Mursil Prophets is the Siwak (brushing of the teeth with a twig).

key_terms.السِّوَاكُ: The act of cleaning teeth with a twig, a prophetic practice
key_terms.سُنَنِ: Plural of Sunnah, meaning established traditions or practices

ai.seo_question: What is the religious significance of using Siwak in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi explicitly categorizes Siwak as a 'Sunnah of the Prophets' (Sunan al-Mursalin), linking the physical act of oral hygiene to the spiritual continuity of prophetic tradition. In Shia scholarship, this elevates Siwak from mere hygiene to a recommended act of worship (Mustahabb) that embodies both physical purity and spiritual readiness for prayer. The chain of narration underscores the reliability of this practice within the Imami tradition, connecting the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) directly to the Imams through a robust isnad.
